erase.stays: The items, shops and barcodes you added to the shared catalogue stay, without your name. One number stays too: how many people who came in the same week deleted their data.
erase.devices: What is saved on this device is erased. Copies on other devices stay until the app or the site data is deleted there.
erase.final: This cannot be undone. You can download a copy first: «Download my data».

erase.signed_out: This sign-in has already ended, and this tap deleted nothing. If you have already deleted your data — here, in the bot or on another device — it is gone; if not, sign in and delete it again.
erase.unknown: We do not know whether the data was deleted: the answer to the last tap was lost, and the sign-in is gone.

privacy.title: Data and privacy
privacy.summary: Your list of purchases is shown to nobody. Others see only prices — without your name and only in a shop where at least three people bought the item — and ratings only as an average of three people. No ads, no trackers, no analytics.

telegram.text: To recognise you on any device. Your name, username and photo are not kept.

purchases.text: What, where, when and for how much. This is the most personal part: it shows where you go. Only you see your list of purchases. Others may see a price you paid, without your name and only in a shop where at least three people bought that item — then the lowest price may turn out to be yours.

exchanges.text: How much you changed, of which currency and when, and the note of where, if you write one — your own rate is worked out from them. When you amend an exchange, the version before it is kept beside it for as long as the exchange itself. Only you see them.

incomes.text: How much came in, in which currency, when and from where, and the note if you write one — your rate is worked out from these too. When you amend an income, the earlier version is kept beside it for as long as the income exists. Only you see it.

spendings.text: How much, in what, when, in which category, and «what» and «where» if you write them — and your own categories. Spending in another currency keeps the rate of its day, and a past month the rate of its last day, worked out from your exchanges. Only you see it.

receipts.text: The photo of a receipt you sent and what was read from it: the shop’s taxpayer number, the date, the lines and the total. Our own server reads it; no outside service sees the receipt. The photo is deleted as soon as you record the receipt, and a receipt left unrecorded goes whole 28 days after it was sent. The item lines cut out of the photo (without the head, where your name may be printed, and without the total) are kept no longer than 28 days after recording — recognition learns from them. If you left the screen while a receipt was being read, the Molvia bot tells you in Telegram that it is ready: the message names the shop or the receipt’s date and the number of items — no sums, no products — and Telegram sees that message. Kept here: how you learned the receipt was ready — in the app or from the bot — and whether that message is off.

accounts.text: An account’s name, its currency, the «savings» mark, the balance on its start day and your checks against the fact — what you counted and what the app counted; for spending, income, exchanges and purchases — which account and how much was charged. The balance is not stored but worked out. Only you see it.

places.text: The names of the shops you give with your purchases — in the shared catalogue, without your name.

barcodes.text: A code you linked to an item, and when. The code itself is in the shared catalogue: everyone finds the item by it, but whose it is is shown to nobody.

ratings.text: Only you see your review. Others see a rating only inside an average of three people.

reminders.text: When the bot last reminded you to rate your purchases, and which reminder in a row it was — so that it writes less often if you do not answer. And whether the reminders are off — by you, or because you blocked the bot — and since when the bot is blocked. The message itself carries the item and the shop to Telegram: otherwise the question would not say what it is about.

feedback.text: What you wrote in «Write to the developer» or in reply to the developer’s answer in the Molvia bot, its kind, and what goes with the text: the app version, the screen, the phone’s system and whether it is the app or a browser, the language, and from an error screen its code. Screenshots, if you attached them yourself: everything in the file but the picture is removed before it is sent, where it was taken included. A screenshot is kept only until it reaches the developer in Telegram, and no longer than a week; Telegram sees it, as it sees the text, and a copy stays in the developer’s chat. And the developer’s replies, each with the number of the Telegram message it reached you as: that is how your answer joins the same conversation. Only the developer reads them. A copy of the message reaches the developer in Telegram without your name or account number, and stays in that chat even after the message is deleted here. Kept for a year from the last message of the conversation.

search.text: What you took for which query, so that next time it comes first. And a query that found nothing, if you then found the item by another word — so that next time your word finds it. Only you see this.

visits.text: Whether you opened “What to buy” — at most once a day. This is how we learn whether people come back. You can turn them off in the settings, “Count me in the statistics”: past marks are deleted at once, no new ones are written, and you are no longer counted in whether people use Molvia — by marks or by ratings.

devices.text: The name of the phone and browser you signed in from, and when you last used them. The list is in Settings, under Devices, where any sign-in can be ended. A sign-in unused for six months is deleted by itself.

settings.text: Country, city, currencies, and the day you changed the currency of conversion — and for “Count me in the statistics”: since when it is off, and when you last turned it back on.

consent.text: Which edition of the Terms of use and of this page you accepted, and when — so that we can ask you again when they change in a way that matters. We keep neither your age nor your date of birth.

logs.title: Server logs
logs.text: Kept for no longer than 14 days. Requests are written to them without your IP address and without what you searched for. An IP address can reach only the server's error log — and it too lives there no longer than 14 days.

failures.title: App failures
failures.text: When something in the app breaks, the phone sends the developer the kind of error, the screen it happened on, the app version and the phone’s system — none of your data: not what you typed, not your purchases, not your account. The phone’s address is not recorded. With no connection it waits on the phone. Kept for 30 days.

backups.title: Where the data and its copies are
backups.text: The server is in Germany, with the host Contabo. Once a day the database is copied, encrypted, to Cloudflare storage in the EU; only the owner of Molvia can decrypt a copy. Copies live 14 days — fourteen days after erasure your data is gone from them too. If the server ever has to be restored from a copy, an erasure made less than a day before the failure may need repeating. Receipt photos, the lines cut out of them and the screenshots sent to the developer are not copied.

barcodes.title: An unknown barcode
barcodes.text: If the catalogue does not know a scanned code, the server asks Open Food Facts, an open database of products, about it. Only the code itself and our server's address go there: not you, not your phone and not your sign-in. A shop's own label code never goes there. The name and size from there are only a hint, which you confirm or correct; items suggested with a code Open Food Facts knows are marked. The link «Data from Open Food Facts» opens the product's page there — from your phone, when you tap it. Open Food Facts data is open under the ODbL licence: we will send an export of what the catalogue took from there on request.

storage.title: Cookies and the phone's memory
storage.text: Two cookies: the sign-in, and one more for five minutes while you sign in. The phone keeps what you saw last and what has not reached the server yet. All of it is needed for the app to work, so there is no banner. Signing out in Settings erases all of it from the phone.

copy.title: A copy of your data
copy.text: In the settings — «Download my data»: a file with everything about you in the database, including the earlier versions of exchanges and incomes you corrected, the items you added to the shared catalogue, the barcodes you linked, the receipts read — without their photos — and your messages to the developer — without their screenshots. A rating you withdrew is there too: without its review it stays with us, so the count of ratings given stays honest. What you removed and can still bring back is there as well, marked. The file holds no login keys.

erase.title: Delete everything
erase.text: In Settings, «Delete my data», or send /delete to the bot you sign in with and confirm. Data is deleted from the database immediately and for good, and from the backups within 14 days: everything in the list above goes except the shops — they, the items you added to the shared catalogue and the barcodes you linked stay, without your name. Deleting from Settings also erases the copies on the phone you deleted from; on other devices, and after /delete, they may remain: to remove them, delete the app there or clear the site's data — or sign out there in Settings beforehand. You can sign in again, but it will be a new, empty account. One number without a name remains after deletion: how many people who came in the same week as you deleted their data. It is there so that whether Molvia gets used is counted honestly.

what.title: What this is
what.text: Molvia is an app where people note what is worth buying, and where. One person makes it. It is not a shop and not an advertisement.

who.title: Who may use it
who.text: You must be 16 or older. You sign in with your Telegram — there is no other way.

yours.title: Your records
yours.text: Your purchases, spendings, exchanges and accounts are seen by you alone. Others see ratings and prices without a name, and only once at least three people have recorded them. In detail — «Data and privacy».

write.title: What to write
write.text: What you bought and tried yourself. Do not write what you know to be false, or anyone else’s personal data — not in names, not in notes, not in messages to the developer.

catalogue.title: The shared catalogue
catalogue.text: The items and barcodes you add become part of the shared catalogue and stay in it without your name, even if you delete your account.

ads.title: No advertising
ads.text: There is no advertising and no paid placement in the answers — not now, not later.

warranty.title: No warranty
warranty.text: Ratings are people’s opinions, prices are what they recorded. The app is provided as is. What to buy is your decision.

free.title: Your own is free
free.text: Recording and seeing your own data is free, always. If access to other people’s figures ever becomes paid, a new edition will appear here, and the app will ask you again.

changes.title: Deletion and changes
changes.text: You can delete everything at any time: in Settings, or with /delete in the bot. If the terms or «Data and privacy» change in a way that matters, the app will ask for your consent again the next time you open it.

consent.title: Terms and privacy
consent.body: Your purchases are seen by you alone. Others see prices and ratings without a name — and only once at least three people have recorded them. No ads, no trackers.

error.body: The receipt is safe. Any line edits are kept on this phone

line.title: Receipt line
line.check_warn: Not a sure match: the receipt says “{text}”. Check the item or pick another
line.name: Name it
line.name_note: The catalogue has no such item — saving adds it
line.price: Price for all, as on the receipt
line.weight_hint: {qty} × {price} — we work out the unit price
line.mismatch: The receipt says {printed} for this line, but {qty} × {price} is {sum}. Fix the price or quantity — or leave it: it doesn’t stop saving
line.remembered: Last time it was {price} here — check the digits
line.skipped: This line isn’t saved. It stays in the receipt sum — it was paid for

pick.title: Pick an item
pick.keep_new_note: Saving adds it to the catalogue
pick.note: Items come from the catalogue only: the same Save button adds a new one
pick.bad_name: This name won’t do — make it shorter

place.title: Where was it?
place.missing: The place wasn’t read on the receipt
place.name: Shop

recorded.title: Saved {n} purchase | Saved {n} purchases
recorded.body: Rate them at home, in Ratings. Any line can be fixed right now too
recorded.printed_note: Grey under each purchase — the line as printed. The photo is deleted

failed.title: Couldn’t read it
failed.body: The lines in the photo can’t be made out — faint print and glare do that. Add the purchases by hand or retake the receipt.
failed.reshoot_body: Retake the receipt or add the purchases by hand. What helps most: the receipt filling the frame — in parts if it is long; flattened with your palm; no shadow of your hand or phone.
failed.manual_body: The lines in the photo can’t be made out. You can record the purchases by hand.
failed.photos_elsewhere: The photo was taken on another phone — it isn’t here

duplicate.title: This receipt was saved on {day}
duplicate.body: It has the same number as a saved one. No need to save it twice — you can delete this one with its photo.

gone.title: This receipt is gone
gone.body: It was deleted — perhaps on another phone.
